findings.text: `holder = lease.holder()` refuses a lease older than LEASE_STALE_SECONDS (reckon/crew/host_lease.py:16, 30s) even when the recorded process still runs — a state host_lease.py:127 documents as normal when a busy holder's renewing thread waits on the interpreter. station_pid_on_this_host therefore returns None during a stalled renewal, pid_belongs_to_the_station returns False, and read_pointer at runs.py:1195 stops dropping the station's pid, restoring the fail-open this section exists to close: crew stop and crew discard can then signal the station and with it every session's fleet. The pre-repair reader at f23de4dd had no staleness test, so the repair narrows the guard it was landed to keep.

station_lease_path lost its only caller when station_pid_on_this_host was rewritten (f23de4dd runs.py:1112 called it; the new body calls _station_lease at 1127) and a tree-wide grep finds the definition alone, so the module keeps a dead public helper.
